question.text: Liquid oxygen at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> is heated to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>300</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> at a constant pressure of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>atm</mi></math>. The rate of heating is constant. Among the following graphs that represent the variation of temperature with time is

solution.text: Temperature of liquid oxygen will first increase in the same phase. Then, phase change ( liquid to gas) will take place. During which temperature will remain constant. After that temperature of oxygen in gaseous state will further increase.
